name: Simon Magus
charge: Offering money for the gift of the Holy Ghost
summary: A certain man called Simon had used sorcery in Samaria and gave out that he was some great one, and all gave heed to him, from the least to the greatest, calling him the great power of God. When Philip preached, Simon believed and was baptized and kept company with him, wondering at the miracles. Then he saw the Holy Ghost given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands and offered them money for the same power, and Peter told him his heart was not right and that he was in the gall of bitterness and the bond of iniquity. He was commanded to repent and pray, and he asked the apostles to pray for him.
offenseFull: Before Philip came down to Samaria there was a certain man called Simon who used sorcery and bewitched the people, giving out that he himself was some great one, and they all gave heed to him, from the least to the greatest, saying that this man was the great power of God, because of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries (Acts 8:9-11). That bewitching is what Christianity does to our people today, a binding spell that covers the eyes from seeing the truth, where a man can read the plain scripture that Christ is black and that he came first to the lost sheep of the house of Israel, and walk away not believing, or say he does not want the Bible, only your opinion, and then reject that too. It is an enchantment to the highest level, where a man reads one thing in front of him and sees something else. Then the people believed Philip and were baptized, both men and women, and Simon himself believed also and was baptized and continued with Philip, wondering at the miracles and signs (Acts 8:12-13).

The apostles at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word and sent Peter and John, who prayed for them and laid their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost (Acts 8:14-17). Notice the order: Philip the deacon woke the city up and planted, but the apostles had to come and put the spirit on them, the same order kept today when the bishop and the apostles visit the cities where new schools open and pray over the congregation. Paul described that order when he said he planted and Apollos watered, but God gave the increase (1 Corinthians 3:6). What those men received with the laying on of hands was the spirit and the remission of sins, because Christ appeared once in the end of the world to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself (Hebrews 9:26). When Simon saw that the Holy Ghost was given through the laying on of the apostles’ hands, he offered them money and asked for the same power, that on whomever he laid hands the man might receive the Holy Ghost (Acts 8:18-19). Simon had the spirits of covetousness, envy, preeminence, and vainglory. He had held status as the great power of God, and when he lost it those spirits rose up in him and he wanted to buy back what he once had, thinking, I have the money, I will pay you for what you have. His art was itself forbidden in Israel, which suffers no enchanter or user of divination among the people (Deuteronomy 18:10-11).
judgmentFull: Peter answered that his money would perish with him because he had thought the gift of God could be purchased with money, that he had neither part nor lot in the matter because his heart was not right, and that he should repent and pray, for Peter perceived he was in the gall of bitterness and in the bond of iniquity (Acts 8:20-23). The gall of bitterness is deep resentment and bitterness of spirit; the bond of iniquity is sin holding a man fast. It was a foolish thought in his head, that the spirit of God could be bought. Simon became jealous because the signs God worked through the apostles overshadowed what the people had known him for. That thing did not come overnight. He fed envy, preeminence, vainglory, and covetousness day by day until the roots of bitterness took hold and bound him, and he became a prisoner of his own mind, trapped and sinning.

Simon answered and asked them to pray to the Lord for him, that none of the things they had spoken would come upon him (Acts 8:24-25). This is why, when people come into the truth, some who had status, fame, or money as celebrities, pastors, or deacons have to come up as a member and clean themselves. Some get jealous, hold on to the envy, and try to bring different doctrines to sway members away, the same spirit of bitterness that moved the Pharisees to kill Christ because the disciples came from nowhere and went to the scriptures better without the status. The history outside the Bible says Simon Magus followed Peter performing tricks and became known as the father of heretics, teaching salvation by grace alone without works and claiming that he had manifested himself as the father in Samaria, the son in Judaea, and the holy spirit to the Gentiles, making himself a trinity. The validity of that account is uncertain, but some of our brothers recover themselves, and this one, by that record, never did.

lawsResolved.text: Do not try to purchase gifts of God with money and offerings.
Witchcraft, wizardry, and sorcery condemned and forbidden to be practice.
The love of money is the root of all evil, and causes one to wander from the faith.
Priests are not to teach or instruct for hire or for a price.
Unless you repent you will perish.

text.text: But there was a certain man, called Simon, which beforetime in the same city used sorcery, and bewitched the people of Samaria, giving out that himself was some great one:
To whom they all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God.
And to him they had regard, because that of long time he had bewitched them with sorceries.
But when they believed Philip preaching the things concerning the kingdom of God, and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
Then Simon himself believed also: and when he was baptized, he continued with Philip, and wondered, beholding the miracles and signs which were done.
Now when the apostles which were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent unto them Peter and John:
Who, when they were come down, prayed for them, that they might receive the Holy Ghost:
(For as yet he was fallen upon none of them: only they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.)
Then laid they their hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.
I have planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
For then must he often have suffered since the foundation of the world: but now once in the end of the world hath he appeared to put away sin by the sacrifice of himself.
And when Simon saw that through laying on of the apostles’ hands the Holy Ghost was given, he offered them money,
Saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay hands, he may receive the Holy Ghost.
There shall not be found among you any one that maketh his son or his daughter to pass through the fire, or that useth divination, or an observer of times, or an enchanter, or a witch,
Or a charmer, or a consulter with familiar spirits, or a wizard, or a necromancer.
But Peter said unto him, Thy money perish with thee, because thou hast thought that the gift of God may be purchased with money.
Thou hast neither part nor lot in this matter: for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.
Repent therefore of this thy wickedness, and pray God, if perhaps the thought of thine heart may be forgiven thee.
For I perceive that thou art in the gall of bitterness, and in the bond of iniquity.
Then answered Simon, and said, Pray ye to the Lord for me, that none of these things which ye have spoken come upon me.
And they, when they had testified and preached the word of the Lord, returned to Jerusalem, and preached the gospel in many villages of the Samaritans.
Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.

And he returned to the man of God, he and all his company, and came, and stood before him: and he said, Behold, now I know that there is no God in all the earth, but in Israel: now therefore, I pray thee, take a blessing of thy servant.
But he said, As the Lord liveth, before whom I stand, I will receive none. And he urged him to take it; but he refused.

The heads thereof judge for reward, and the priests thereof teach for hire, and the prophets thereof divine for money: yet will they lean upon the Lord, and say, Is not the Lord among us? none evil can come upon us.
